record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.context_brief: Frostman-type approximation for Bergman inner divisors
record.original_question: Let M(H2, L2_a) be the multiplier space from H2(D) to L2_a(D), with norm ||G|| = sup{||Gf||_L2: f in H2(D), ||f||_H2 ≤ 1}. Is every inner divisor for L2_a(D) approximable by zero divisors in this multiplier norm?

evidence.quote: Let M(H2, L2_a) be the space of multipliers H2(D) -> L2_a(D), normed appropriately: ||G|| = sup {||Gf||_L2 : f ∈ H2(D), ||f||_H2 ≤ 1}.
Conjecture 6.2. Every inner divisor for L2_a(D) is approximable by zero divisors in the norm of M(H2, L2_a).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk. Let $H^2(\mathbb{D})$ be the classical Hardy space of holomorphic functions $f$ on $\mathbb{D}$ with $\|f\|_{H^2}^2=\sup_{0<r<1}\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}|f(re^{i\theta})|^2\,d\theta<\infty$, and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ be the Bergman space of holomorphic functions on $\mathbb{D}$ with $\|f\|_{L^2_a}^2=\int_{\mathbb{D}}|f(z)|^2\,dA(z)<\infty$, where $dA$ is normalized area measure.

Define the multiplier space
$$M(H^2,L^2_a)=\{G\text{ holomorphic on }\mathbb{D}: Gf\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})\text{ for all }f\in H^2(\mathbb{D})\},$$
endowed with the norm $\|G\|=\sup\{\|Gf\|_{L^2_a}:f\in H^2(\mathbb{D}),\ \|f\|_{H^2}\le 1\}$.

For a nonzero closed (invariant) subspace $I\subset L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ that is invariant under multiplication by $z$, the associated extremal function $G_I\in I$ — characterized as the solution of an extremal problem — is called the inner divisor of $I$. When $I$ is the subspace of all functions in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ vanishing on a given $L^2_a$-zero set, the corresponding extremal function is called a zero divisor.

Question: Is every inner divisor for $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ approximable, in the norm of $M(H^2,L^2_a)$, by zero divisors of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search returns related work on contractive zero divisors and inner functions in Bergman spaces (Hedenmalm; Duren–Khavinson–Shapiro–Sundberg), but no source was found that explicitly resolves the multiplier-norm Frostman-type approximation conjecture for inner divisors of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$. Current status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Bergman-Type Reproducing Kernels, Contractive Divisors, and Dilations
status_evidence.snippet: Hedenmalm proved the existence of a canonical contractive zero-divisor playing the role of a Blaschke product in the Bergman space; Duren, Khavinson, Shapiro, and Sundberg extended this to L^p_α.
status_evidence.claim: Contractive zero-divisor theory in Bergman spaces is developed, but no explicit resolution of the multiplier-norm approximation conjecture appears.

status_evidence.title: Contractive Zero–Divisors in Bergman Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of contractive zero divisors in Bergman spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature on zero divisors does not address the specific Frostman-type multiplier approximation question.
